The Prophet returned the wild ass, or game meat, given him while in ihram, telling al-Sa'b b. Jaththama it was refused only because they were in ihram.
Pilgrims in ihram could eat the wild ass Abu Qatada hunted out of ihram, as none of them had pointed or helped, and the Prophet ate some; Talha approved likewise.
Game from a trained dog sent with Allah's name is lawful unless it ate or another dog joined; game hit flat by a blunt arrow, or found drowned, is not.
The People of the Book's vessels may be used, washed, only when no others exist; game taken with Allah's name may be eaten even three days later if not rotten.
The Prophet forbade flinging pebbles, which neither catch game nor defeat an enemy but break teeth and put out eyes; Ibn Mughaffal would not speak to one who persisted.
